feature: Switching the history filter answers within a frame
summary: Clicking All, Screenshots or Videos in the history bar no longer holds the app: the filter shows your pick on the next frame and the new strip a frame after, every frame under 16ms (it was 40 to 110ms). Walking the strip with the arrow keys is smoother too.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Best with a big Screenshots folder (the walk uses a made-up history of 500 captures, one in three a recording).

try.do: Press Shift-Command-H to open the history bar.
Click Screenshots, then Videos, then All, quickly, several times over.
Press the right arrow thirty or forty times to walk well along the strip.
Click Videos: the newest recordings show at the start, at once.
Click All: it is back at its start with the newest capture ringed.
Hold the right arrow down for a second and watch the ring and the strip move.

evaluate: Does a click on the filter feel instant now, with no catch before the strip changes?
Does the chip still slide across the filter the way it did, with nothing jumping?
Does the strip you come back to always start at the newest capture?
Do the arrow keys move the ring without a stutter near the start of the strip?
rough: The answer comes over three short frames rather than one: the filter's words change the frame after the click, then the chip sets off and the strip changes. At 60Hz that is all within about 33ms.
Opening the bar still takes one long frame of 85 to 125ms, as before this change; after it, the two strips not in sight are built in the background, one frame of about 35ms each, while nothing moves.
Arrow steps read 7ms typically and up to about 14ms; the first steps after a switch are the slowest.
No visual change was intended: the bar and strip look as they did on 2026-09-30.
